narrator.instruct: Fast-paced, energetic, punchy explainer narrator. Brisk delivery with no long pauses.

neighbour.instruct: Flustered, slightly out of breath neighbour in a bathrobe, surprised and talkative.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You sprint onto the platform just as your train pulls away.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your phone says you're late. Your oven clock swore you had time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That oven clock has never been wrong.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Each week your mornings feel calmer. You're winning.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then your neighbour knocks, holding up his radio alarm clock.

lines.speaker: neighbour
lines.text: Is yours slow too? Mine's six minutes behind!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So are millions of clocks across Europe.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your phone keeps its own time. These clocks don't.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They count the electricity coming out of the wall.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The current swings back and forth fifty times a second.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Fifty swings, one tick. That's the whole clock.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Twenty-five countries share that one rhythm, from Spain to Turkey.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It stays at fifty only if power in matches power out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In early twenty eighteen, two Balkan grid operators fell into a dispute.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Kosovo's grid was short of power, and Serbia's operator didn't fill the gap.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the whole grid ran at about forty-nine point nine nine six.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Each second, your oven lost a sliver.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: From January to March, the slivers added up to almost six minutes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In March, operators pushed extra energy in to run it slightly fast.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By April, the oven clocks had quietly caught up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your neighbour is still resetting his radio.
